title: Dynamic thresholds and spatial boundaries coordinate memory association and discrimination across scales
title_zh: 动态阈值与空间边界在不同尺度上协调记忆关联与辨别
abstract: The ability to connect related experiences while preserving their individual identities is a central requirement of adaptive behavior. Engram overlap offers a cellular substrate for memory linking, but overlap must be regulated: too little prevents integration, whereas too much promotes generalization, interference, and confusion. Here, we organize evidence across molecular, cellular, glial, circuit, and systems levels around a common association-discrimination problem. We distinguish prospective linking, in which temporally adjacent experiences are biased toward shared neuronal allocation during a transient excitability window, from retrospective linking, in which memories separated in time are integrated through replay and cross-regional coordination. Within this framework, CREB- and CCR5-associated excitability states and inhibitory microcircuits set dynamic thresholds that regulate the timing and extent of neuronal recruitment; dendritic compartmentalization and branch-specific plasticity help preserve event-specific information within shared neurons; and representational drift may provide temporal decorrelation across repeated experiences. We further evaluate emerging evidence that learning-associated astrocyte ensembles, perisynaptic processes, calcium dynamics, and metabolic coupling help set the spatial boundaries of plasticity, while emphasizing that a direct role in defining engram boundaries remains a testable hypothesis. Together, these mechanisms form a Memory Engram Association Network that links neural organization to behavioral outcomes including integration, discrimination, generalization, and interference. This framework identifies experimentally separable mechanisms and shows how their disruption may contribute to age- and disease-related cognitive dysfunction. As this evidence is predominantly rodent-derived, we review the human literature on generalization, interference, and integration separately and frame the clinical extensions, including neurorehabilitation, as predictions awaiting human test.
abstract_zh: 连接相关经验同时保留其个体身份是适应性行为的核心需求。记忆痕迹重叠为记忆联结提供了细胞基础，但重叠必须受到调控：过少会阻碍整合，过多则会促进泛化、干扰和混淆。本文在分子、细胞、星形胶质细胞、回路和系统层面上整合证据，聚焦于共同的关联-辨别问题。我们区分前瞻性联结，即时间相邻的经验在短暂兴奋窗口内被偏向共享神经元分配；以及回顾性联结，即时间分隔的记忆通过重放和跨区域协调实现整合。在此框架下，CREB 与 CCR5 相关的兴奋状态和抑制微回路设定动态阈值，调控神经元招募的时机与范围；树突分区化与分支特异性可塑性帮助在共享神经元中保留事件特异信息；而表征漂移可能为重复经验提供时间去相关化。我们进一步评估新兴证据，指出学习相关星形胶质细胞集群、突触周围过程、钙动力学和代谢耦合有助于设定可塑性的空间边界，并强调其在定义记忆痕迹边界方面的直接作用仍是可检验的假设。综上，这些机制构成了记忆痕迹关联网络，将神经组织与行为结果（包括整合、辨别、泛化和干扰）联系起来。该框架识别了可实验分离的机制，并展示其破坏如何可能导致与年龄和疾病相关的认知功能障碍。由于这些证据主要来自啮齿动物，我们分别回顾了人类关于泛化、干扰和整合的文献，并将临床延伸（包括神经康复）框定为待验证的人类预测。
